title: Two Ends of the Serpent Column
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Ten claim cards about the Serpent Column, the Plataean victory monument that stood at Delphi and now stands in Istanbul's Hippodrome; the learner drags or assigns each card to one of three bins, Check it at Delphi, Check it in Istanbul, or Only in a written source, then checks all ten with card-level feedback.

educational.topic: The Serpent Column: what Delphi, Istanbul, and the ancient writers each contribute as evidence
learningObjectives: Attribute each of 10 claims about the Serpent Column to the place where its evidence can be checked, at Delphi, in Istanbul, or only in an ancient written source, with at least 8 of 10 correct on the first attempt.
prerequisites: Battle of Plataea and the Persian Wars
Herodotus, Thucydides and Pausanias as sources
Great altar and temple terrace at Delphi

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Attribution sorting into three evidence bins with a single scored first Check, card-level feedback, and unlimited re-checks
keyQuestions: The bronze is in Istanbul. What can only Delphi tell us?
Which claims come from ancient writers rather than from the object or the place?
Why does an object far from home tell only half its story?
commonMisconceptions: Everything about the column can be seen in Istanbul, because the bronze is there.
Delphi has nothing left of the monument.
Facts in a museum label must come from the object itself, when many come from ancient writers.
assessmentOpportunities: First-Check score on ten cards (mastery: 8 of 10).
Explain which parts of the column's story would be lost without Herodotus and Thucydides.
